name: Yunü
description: A star 91 parsecs away, 32 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: radius 31.71 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 260.547 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.064) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: effective temperature 4121 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.079)

gravity.source: SIMBAD's compilation of spectroscopic measurements (mesFe_h): log g 1.59 from 2024A&A...682A.145S; the 6 published values span log g 1.5 to 1.81, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.1% of the centre brightness

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 49637: distance 90.58 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.022), at which the luminosity and radius hold

text.card: A star 91 parsecs away, 32 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 261 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,121 K, so 31.71 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 49637: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: 31 Leonis
quotes.card: 31 Leonis, also named Yunü, is a binary star system in the equatorial constellation of Leo.
quotes.introduction: The system is visible to the naked eye in unresolved form, having a combined apparent visual magnitude of 4.39.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 3879879704937353984 (quality A), from 2005A&A...430..165F; Gaia DR3 measures none
